**Stanley Black & Decker, Inc. - Credit Agreement Amendment No. 1**

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Date of Agreement:** February 23, 2023

**Borrower/Company Overview:** Stanley Black & Decker, Inc., a Connecticut corporation

**Transaction Description:** Amendment No. 1 to an existing $1,500,000,000 364-Day Credit Agreement originally dated September 7, 2022. The transaction involves Stanley Black & Decker, Inc. as borrower, multiple institutional lenders, and Citibank, N.A. as administrative agent.

**Purpose of Financing:** The amendment provides covenant relief by temporarily reducing the Interest Coverage Ratio requirement and allowing significant EBITDA adjustments during specified adjustment periods to accommodate operational challenges and restructuring activities.

**Company Background:** Stanley Black & Decker is an established industrial company that has recently completed acquisitions (MTD Holdings, Inc. and Excel Industries) and is undergoing various operational changes including facility closures, supply chain transformation, business divestments (including Russia business closure), and restructuring activities.

---

## 2. INVESTMENT HIGHLIGHTS & RISKS

### Key Strengths / Credit Positives:
• **Strong Lender Syndicate** - Diverse group of major financial institutions including Citibank, Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, and other tier-1 banks
• **Short-Term Facility** - 364-day term structure limits duration risk
• **Temporary Covenant Relief** - Amendment provides measured relief with clear time boundaries (through Q2 2024)
• **Capped Adjustments** - EBITDA addbacks are limited to $500 million per adjustment period, preventing unlimited adjustments
• **Fee Generation** - Amendment generates 3 basis points amendment fee for participating lenders

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
• **Covenant Relief Necessity** - Company required significant reduction in Interest Coverage Ratio (from 3.50x to 1.50x) indicating potential financial stress
• **Extensive Addback Categories** - Broad range of adjustment categories suggests multiple operational challenges
• **Integration Risks** - Recent acquisitions (MTD Holdings, Excel Industries) create integration execution risk
• **Restructuring Exposure** - Multiple restructuring activities including facility closures and supply chain transformation
• **Geographic Risk** - Russia business closure indicates geopolitical exposure

**Mitigating Factors:** Time-limited covenant relief, capped adjustment amounts, and maintained lender group commitment
